title: Run randomized parallel tests to detect test pollution

note.title: Run randomized parallel tests to detect test pollution
answers: How do I detect tests that pollute other tests?
How do I run Click tests in random order across multiple cores?
Which test environment helps investigate flaky tests and race conditions?
note.body:
Run `tox r -e random` to execute tests in randomized order and in parallel.
The command is defined in `pyproject.toml:tool.tox.env.random` and documented in `docs/contributing.md`.
The environment installs the `tests-random` dependency group, including `pytest-randomly` and `pytest-xdist`.
`--numprocesses=auto` automatically selects the parallel worker count.
`--basetemp={env_tmp_dir}` places pytest temporary files in the tox environment's temporary directory; `-v --tb=short` enables verbose output with short tracebacks.
The command forwards positional arguments to pytest, allowing a narrower test selection.
note.applies: Use the optional random tox environment when checking Click tests for test pollution, flakiness, or race conditions.
